Seorang pria dengan pakaian sederhana dan terlihat lusuh datang ke sebuah kantor perusahaan.

Penampilannya membuat beberapa orang langsung memandangnya sebelah mata.

Saat hendak masuk ke dalam kantor, ia justru dihentikan dan ditolak oleh petugas keamanan.

Alasannya sederhana...

Ia dianggap tidak pantas berada di dalam gedung tersebut.

Pria itu mencoba menjelaskan bahwa dirinya memiliki urusan penting dengan pihak perusahaan. Namun, tidak ada yang mau mendengarkan.

Ia tetap dianggap hanya orang biasa yang mungkin salah tempat.

Tanpa marah dan tanpa membuat keributan, pria tersebut memilih untuk tetap tenang.

Namun, tidak seorang pun menyangka bahwa keputusan mereka menolak pria itu akan menjadi sebuah kesalahan besar.

Karena pria yang mereka anggap tidak penting tersebut ternyata memiliki hubungan yang sangat besar dengan perusahaan itu.

🔥 DIA BUKAN ORANG BIASA.

Pria berpenampilan lusuh itu ternyata adalah INVESTOR TERBESAR perusahaan tersebut!

Bagaimana reaksi mereka ketika identitas sebenarnya mulai terungkap?

Apa yang akan terjadi kepada orang-orang yang sebelumnya menolak dan meremehkannya?

Dan mengapa seorang investor besar datang ke kantor dengan pakaian sesederhana itu?

👉 Saksikan sampai akhir untuk mengetahui alasan di balik penyamarannya dan bagaimana semuanya berubah setelah identitasnya terungkap.

Cerita ini mengingatkan kita bahwa penampilan bukanlah ukuran kesuksesan seseorang.

Jangan pernah meremehkan orang hanya karena pakaian, pekerjaan, atau penampilannya.

Karena kita tidak pernah tahu siapa sebenarnya orang yang sedang berdiri di hadapan kita.

snippet.title: This made-in-India robot is unstoppable
snippet.description:
Strider Robotics is the oldest continuously operational group developing quadruped robots in India. They operate out of the ARTPARK at the IISc in Bengaluru. Officially incorporated as a private limited company in 2024, they've developed a line of robotic platforms, progressing through earlier M1 and M2 iterations before arriving at their current prototype, M3.

M3 currently exists as a highly advanced prototype, with commercialisation expected within a matter of months. Structurally, the M3 is engineered as a heavy-duty, high-capacity quadruped rather than a lightweight, high-speed unit. Aditya Varma Sagi has explicitly stated that sheer speed and varied, flashy gaits are not the primary focus of this generation. Instead, the core directive is reliable, safe, point-to-point operation under substantial physical stress. This design philosophy is vividly demonstrated by the platform's exceptional payload capacities. During field demonstrations, M3 is capable of comfortably bearing the full body weight of an adult human while performing completely controlled vertical squats and lifts. Further testing involves strapping 40 kilograms of dead weight directly to the robot's chassis and successfully navigating stairs.

To bridge the gap between laboratory conditions and real-world deployment, Strider rigorously tests the M3 outside the controlled confines of indoor environments, exposing the platform to the unpredictable elements of the IISc ARTPARK campus. The quadruped demonstrates remarkable stability across varied topographies, effortlessly handling loose soil, exposed tree roots, uneven ground, and small outdoor steps. The robot is also equipped with advanced dynamic recovery protocols. If the M3 loses its footing or is knocked over on uneven outdoor terrain, it can autonomously articulate its limbs to right itself and return to a standing operational posture without requiring human intervention.

Environmental hardening is another major vector of ongoing development for the M3 platform. Currently, the robot boasts an Ingress Protection rating of IP54. This classification ensures that the complex internal electronics, motors, and computational hardware are protected against fine dust, as well as light water sprays or rain sprinkles. This baseline durability prevents functional disruption during standard outdoor operations, though the engineering team is actively working to elevate the platform to an IP67 rating, which would render it entirely dust-tight and capable of surviving temporary submersion in water. Alongside environmental sealing, the team is actively refining the platform's acoustic signature. Earlier iterations of Strider's quadrupeds relied on chain-based mechanisms that inherently generated significant mechanical noise. The current prototype still produces a noticeable audio footprint primarily caused by the physical rattling of its metallic battery casing against the chassis.

If the M3 loses its footing or is knocked over on uneven outdoor terrain, it can autonomously articulate its limbs to right itself and return to a standing operational posture without requiring human intervention.

Environmental hardening is another major vector of ongoing development for the M3 platform. Currently, the robot boasts an Ingress Protection rating of IP54. This classification ensures that the complex internal electronics, motors, and computational hardware are protected against fine dust, as well as light water sprays or rain sprinkles. This baseline durability prevents functional disruption during standard outdoor operations, though the engineering team is actively working to elevate the platform to an IP67 rating, which would render it entirely dust-tight and capable of surviving temporary submersion in water. Alongside environmental sealing, the team is actively refining the platform's acoustic signature. Earlier iterations of Strider's quadrupeds relied on chain-based mechanisms that inherently generated significant mechanical noise. The current prototype still produces a noticeable audio footprint primarily caused by the physical rattling of its metallic battery casing against the chassis.

snippet.description:
Have you ever stood up after sitting still and felt tingling, numbness, or “pins and needles” in your leg? This temporary sensation can happen when your position puts pressure on a nerve or nearby blood vessels. Changing position and taking the pressure off usually makes it go away. �

In this video, we explain why a hand or foot can feel like it has “fallen asleep” and when to pay closer attention. If tingling keeps coming back or lasts a long time, speak with a healthcare professional.

snippet.title: Smart #2: Why Bigger Isn't Always Better
snippet.description:
Smart is finally making a Smart car again.

This is the new Smart #2 – a tiny two-seat electric city car that's just 2.75 metres long, rear-wheel drive and designed to bring the Smart brand back to its roots.

After years of increasingly large SUVs, Smart has gone back to the idea that made the original City Coupe and Fortwo so brilliant: make it small, fun, distinctive and incredibly easy to drive around town.

The #2 gets a 35.8kWh LFP battery, with Smart targeting up to 180 miles of range. It can charge from 10–80% in around 20 minutes at up to 65kW, while higher-spec versions get 11kW AC charging. There's also Vehicle-to-Load capability.

And despite its tiny dimensions, Smart hasn't exactly skimped on the technology. There's adaptive cruise control, Highway Assist, Smart Pilot Assist, LED lighting and plenty of connectivity, while the Premium version adds heated seats, a glass roof and a seven-speaker Sennheiser sound system.

Underneath, it's rear-wheel drive with an 82hp motor, wider rear tyres and – remarkably – a five-link rear suspension setup.
There are three versions planned for the UK: Pure, Premium and a limited-run Couture Edition, with the #2 expected to cost less than £20,000 when it arrives early next year.

That's potentially cheaper than you might expect for a car that feels more like a modern interpretation of the original Smart than another anonymous electric hatchback.
So has Smart finally found its sense of humour again? And would you actually buy a two-seat electric car in 2027?

snippet.description:
A Ukrainian drone strike has hit a Yandex data centre in Russia’s Vladimir region, the third such facility targeted within days, following earlier attacks near Moscow and in the Ryazan region. The company says no one was injured, though the site reportedly houses key supercomputers used in developing its artificial intelligence systems. The strikes have disrupted services relied upon by millions of Russians, including taxi-hailing, food delivery, cloud computing and navigation tools, with users reporting widespread outages.

Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova reports from Moscow, Russia.

snippet.title: La Mesa de Hora 25 (12/10/2026) | El fallo del Supremo con la ley de nietos y la unión de izquierdas
snippet.description:
Con Berna González Harbour, Cristina Monge y Lourdes Pérez. El Tribunal Supremo ha fallado mantener las medidas cautelares que impiden votar a los nacionalizados con la ley de nietos, del 2022, pese a que sí participaron en anteriores elecciones. Esta decisión afecta "potencialmente" a todos los españoles residentes fuera, tal y como explica la presidenta del Consejo General de la Ciudadanía Española. Además, el PP pide la dimisión del alcalde de Algeciras, ex de este partido, por una nueva denuncia por agresión sexual. Y entrevista a Antonio Maíllo, que confía en que las izquierdas vayan juntas a las elecciones, defiende a Colau como candidata y no se muestra sorprendido por la decisión de Rufián.

Ao lado do governador Tarcísio de Freitas e do prefeito Ricardo Nunes, o candidato prometeu reduzir R$ 250 bilhões em gastos públicos, mas descartou cortes em programas sociais.

Segundo Flávio, a economia viria do combate à corrupção e ao desperdício, sem detalhamento das medidas que seriam adotadas.
